snippet.title: Did Saina Nehwal Manifest Her Own Destiny? #shorts
snippet.description:
What makes someone a champion? Is it years of discipline, relentless hard work, divine intervention, or a little bit of everything?

In this episode of the show, Dr. Jai Madaan sits down with Saina Nehwal, one of India's most celebrated badminton players, for a deeply personal conversation about her extraordinary journey.

From becoming the World No. 1 in badminton to winning an Olympic bronze medal, Saina opens up about the sacrifices her parents made, the discipline it took to compete against the world's best, and the moments on court that felt almost magical.

She also talks about her spiritual connection with Lord Shiva, her experiences at Amarnath and Kedarnath, overcoming a career-threatening knee injury, and finding the mental strength to make a comeback when everything seemed uncertain.

Beyond badminton, Saina gets candid about marriage, relationships, family, motherhood, changing generations and why she believes a strong marriage requires everyday effort.

A conversation about ambition, faith, resilience and the unseen forces that shape our journeys.

Watch till the end to discover the side of Saina Nehwal that goes beyond the champion we know.

snippet.title: Earth Is Closest to the Sun in January!
snippet.description:
Earth is closest to the Sun in early January - in the middle of northern winter. Neil deGrasse Tyson explains why the distance barely matters and the tilt does. Neil deGrasse Tyson on StarTalk ("Why We Have Seasons"). Clip used for commentary; the 3D animations are original.

For the record: perihelion falls around January 3, about 91.4 million miles (147.1 million km) from the Sun; aphelion around July 4, about 94.5 million miles (152.1 million km). Seasons come from Earth's 23.4-degree axial tilt.

snippet.title: How Big Was Garuda? Jatayu's Uncle Carried an Elephant in One Claw
snippet.description:
In Ramayana Part 1 we saw Jatayu fight Ravana. But Valmiki says Jatayu's uncle was Garuda (Aranya Kanda 14: Vinata's sons were Garuda and Aruna, and Jatayu is Aruna's son).

The Mahabharata (Adi Parva 29-30) says Garuda carried an elephant 6 yojanas tall in one claw and a tortoise 3 yojanas tall in the other, then landed on a banyan branch 100 yojanas long, and it snapped. He caught it in his beak, with the sages hanging from it, and flew on.
At ~13 km per yojana, and an eagle's foot being about 1/5 of its body, Garuda comes out around 250 km long with ~650 km wings (our estimate).

How big must Lord Vishnu be, riding him? Comment below.

Watch next: Who Defeated Rama TWICE? Indrajit, Ravana's Son: https://youtu.be/zKtBq1SJDw4
Sources: K. M. Ganguli's Mahabharata; M. N. Dutt's Valmiki Ramayana.

In Ramayana Part 1 we saw Jatayu fight Ravana. But Valmiki says Jatayu's uncle was Garuda (Aranya Kanda 14: Vinata's sons were Garuda and Aruna, and Jatayu is Aruna's son).

The Mahabharata (Adi Parva 29-30) says Garuda carried an elephant 6 yojanas tall in one claw and a tortoise 3 yojanas tall in the other, then landed on a banyan branch 100 yojanas long, and it snapped. He caught it in his beak, with the sages hanging from it, and flew on.
At ~13 km per yojana, and an eagle's foot being about 1/5 of its body, Garuda comes out around 250 km long with ~650 km wings (our estimate).

How big must Lord Vishnu be, riding him? Comment below.

Sources: K. M. Ganguli's Mahabharata; M. N. Dutt's Valmiki Ramayana.
